newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STOCKS SEEN HIT BY U.S. MARKETS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STOCKS SEEN HIT BY U.S. MARKETS.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to fall sharply at the opening Friday tracking the U.S. markets, dealers said.

"It will be a difficult opening. The bolsa will dragged down by ADRs which in turn are reacting to the situation abroad, where U.S. long bond yields have jumped back up to 6.6 percent," said Pablo Cubela at traders Tutelar.

The bolsa had run out of steam Thursday, when the weighted MerVal index .MERV pulled back 0.9 percent to 849.88 against a session ceiling of 860, which would have set a new five-year high. It pared gains so far in the week to 1.1 percent.
Traders said they expected the market to find its feet as soon as volatility ebbed on Wall Street.
"Local company results have been good and unless there is a lasting change of trend in New York, we should switch back to gains shortly," Cubela said.
He noted the fall in U.S. bonds was linked to technical factors stemming from the Treasury's quarterly refunding.
"Bolsa valuations are high so we've come to expect these swings," another dealer said. "But after today's drop prices will be more reasonable and institutional buyers may return."
